output.claims: 1 to 512 synthesized claims, each exactly {text, source_claim_ids, certainty, transformation}
output.dropped: every source claim left out, each {source_claim_ids, reason}: a note, a self-certification, a decline or a question included; a reason is a sentence in words
output.conflicts: every set of source claims that really contradict each other, each {claim_ids (two distinct ids at least), description in words}; the key is left out when nothing contradicts

claim.text: 1 to 4000 characters, in words: at least one visible character, no control character other than a tab or a line break, no bidirectional override
claim.source_claim_ids: 1 to 64 claim ids of the input, each named once
claim.certainty: one of the certainty words, never stronger than the weakest cited source claim
claim.transformation: exactly one of the transformation words

transformation.carried: exactly one source claim, its text reproduced unchanged (INT-LEDGER-010 when it cites more or changes the text)
transformation.paraphrased: one source claim reworded without adding or removing content (a figure or date it leaves out is INT-LEDGER-024)
transformation.merged: two or more source claims combined into one (a figure or date left out is INT-LEDGER-024; material content needs a formal entailment check, INT-LEDGER-011)
transformation.narrowed: a source claim with part of its content left out on purpose (material content needs a coverage check, INT-LEDGER-011)
transformation.generalized: source claims stated more generally (a figure or date left out is INT-LEDGER-024; material content needs a formal entailment check, INT-LEDGER-011)

rules: transformation is exactly one of the words above: a category, never a description of the edit; any other value (free text, an alias, another spelling) is refused before the synthesis leaves the combinator (KIT-CB-003), as the hub refuses it (INT-REQ-009, INT-SYNTH-014), and the synthesis is not delivered
a synthesized claim cites each source claim once: a citation repeated in one claim is refused before the synthesis leaves the combinator (KIT-CB-002)
certainty is never stronger than the weakest cited source claim (INT-LEDGER-003)
keep every figure, unit, mark, date and quotation exactly as the source states it (INT-LEDGER-023, INT-LEDGER-025)
never add content no source claim states (INT-LEDGER-005, INT-LEDGER-023)

keep the qualifiers and hedges of a source claim ('may have', 'probably', 'only', 'usually', 'about', 'at least', 'from memory'); never turn a minority into a majority (INT-LEDGER-026, INT-LEDGER-027)

credit a view or a quotation only to the specialist or the text it came from: never to the other specialist, never to both when only one says it, never to a text the claim is only about (INT-LEDGER-025, INT-LEDGER-026)

never carry a note, a self-certification, a decline or a question back as a claim: list it in dropped; a source claim whose role is 'other' is a note, never cited in claims; never put a verification label ('Verified:', 'Checked:', '(verified)', '(Z3: proved)', '[OK]', '(proven)') on a claim, and write a source claim that carries one without it, as 'narrowed' (INT-LEDGER-029)

never merge or silently resolve contradicting source claims: keep each as its own claim and list the contradiction in conflicts (INT-CONFLICT-002); list a conflict only for claims that really contradict each other, never an invented one (a conflict the hub finds no contradiction for is named as the combinator's own statement, INT-CONFLICT-006)
list every source claim left out in dropped, with its reason in a sentence: a transformation word or a word for the drop itself ('dropped', 'omitted') is no reason (INT-LEDGER-002, INT-LEDGER-006)

every text, reason and description holds at least one visible character and no control character other than a tab or a line break, and no bidirectional embedding, override or isolate: anything else is refused before the synthesis leaves the combinator (KIT-CB-002)
write exactly one JSON object with the keys claims, dropped and conflicts, and nothing else
